narration: You probably picture Noah's ark as an enormous ship. But Genesis describes rooms, three levels, and a coating inside and out. These details are easy to overlook when a single familiar illustration becomes our mental picture. Look closely, and three details become surprisingly difficult to picture. Detail number one: the wood. The text names a material, but its identity is uncertain. Scholars have proposed different woods. An illustrator's confident choice of timber is still a choice, not a recovered construction sample. Detail number two: the layout. Genesis specifies lower, middle, and upper levels, with a door in the side. Imagine a wooden structure divided into compartments, rather than a single open deck with animals lined up for a photograph. The passage gives proportions, but it is not a modern shipbuilder's detailed plan. Detail number three: the coating. The instruction is to cover the structure inside and outside with pitch. That dark layer belongs to the description, not merely an artist's decoration on the outside. Now compare those instructions with the familiar image of a pointed ship beneath a sloping roof. Scholars have traced that common depiction through later interpretations. The passage leaves room for debate about the exact form. We are reading an ancient text, and distinguishing its instructions from the pictures people have built around them. Next time you see Noah's ark, count the levels, check the coating, and ask which details actually come from Genesis. Each image is an interpretation; the short biblical passage is our starting point.
